messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• Exceeding by 5 mph or more is a misdemeanor.
• Exceeding by 10 mph or more is a felony. | Speed limits vary by road type and area. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat. | Failure to buckle up is a misdemeanor. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations are misdemeanors. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08% is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | First offense: $1,000 fine, 90‑day license suspension. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights. | Failure to yield can lead to traffic citations. | | **School‑Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Must remain stopped until the bus resumes motion. | Violations are misdemeanors. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in no‑stop zones, fire lanes, or on sidewalks.
• Parking meters and permit requirements apply in many cities. | Violations can result in fines or towing. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display valid license plates.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Failure to register or inspect can lead to fines and impoundment. | | **Traffic Citations & Penalties** | • Minor infractions: $50–$200 fine.
• Major infractions: $500–$2,000 fine, points on driver’s record. | Points can lead to license suspension after 12 points in 12 months. | **Where to Find Official Sources** | Resource | URL | |----------|-----| | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) – Traffic Rules | https://www.txdmv.gov/ | | Texas Transportation Code (full text) | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ | | Texas Highway Patrol – Enforcement Guidelines | https://www.txdps.state.tx.us/ | **Quick Tips** 1. **Always obey posted speed limits.** Texas has strict penalties for speeding. 2. **Use hands‑free devices only.** Hand‑held phone use is a misdemeanor. 3. **Keep your vehicle registration current.** Out‑of‑state plates can lead to fines. 4. **Check local ordinances.** Cities like Austin and Dallas have additional parking and traffic rules. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular traffic citation!
